coreField.label: Interdisciplinary study of contemporary societal challenges through the intersecting cultural domains of art, science/technology, media and politics
Historical development of Western culture and thought from antiquity to the twenty-first century, tracing the deep historical roots of present-day societal problems
Philosophical, ethical and conceptual analysis of the ideas, norms and values shaping Western culture, and the social and ethical implications of cultural change
Critical, interdisciplinary humanities-and-qualitative-social-science analysis of cultural texts, artefacts, practices, discourses and institutions
Qualitative research methods -- ethnography, discourse analysis, (historical) document analysis and conceptual analysis -- applied to cultural phenomena
Literary and artistic analysis of texts, artworks and cultural representations
Academic writing, structured argumentation and public debate about contemporary cultural and social questions
Independent scholarly research on a self-chosen arts-and-culture topic, culminating in the Bachelor thesis

adjacentDirections.label: Marginalised voices and cultural representation: how the voices and experiences of marginalised groups are represented or excluded in history, public debate and literature
Technology, ethics and the arts: the ethical issues raised by emerging technologies and how art and literature help explore them
Democracy, citizenship and public culture: what it does and could mean to be a democratic society today
Culture and climate change: how scientists, states, activists and industry understand and respond to climate change on a global scale
Bodies, identity and social norms: how social norms about the body are constructed, challenged or transformed

questionsApplications.label: Illustrative or temporary applied formats used to communicate cultural research and analysis (producing a podcast, curating an arts festival, writing a cultural-policy brief)

basisLabels: Historical development of Western culture and thought from antiquity to the twenty-first century, tracing the deep historical roots of present-day societal problems
courseTraceability.rationale: Modern History Provides a chronological overview of history from 1815 to the present. Discusses industrialisation, popular sovereignty and national self‑determination, and covers major economic, political and cultural developments including revolutions, world wars and the fall of communism. Contribution: Partial modern historical context for ideology/modernity; not the full integrated cultural analysis module.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical development of Western culture and thought from antiquity to the twenty-first century, tracing the deep historical roots of present-day societal problems”.

basisLabels: Historical development of Western culture and thought from antiquity to the twenty-first century, tracing the deep historical roots of present-day societal problems

courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Western Philosophy Introduces central themes from Western philosophy over 2,500 years. Encourages inquiry into the significance of philosophical issues and their relation to other disciplines and teaches theoretical methods used by philosophers. Contribution: Partial foundational Western philosophical relationship; UCR broad survey does not reproduce the integrated Maastricht humanities problem/course.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical development of Western culture and thought from antiquity to the twenty-first century, tracing the deep historical roots of present-day societal problems” and “Philosophical, ethical and conceptual analysis of the ideas, norms and values shaping Western culture, and the social and ethical implications of cultural change”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Law, Society & Justice Examines law from legal, socio‑scientific and normative perspectives. Explores definitions, legal traditions and fields of law, investigates the relationship between law and society and the concept of justice, and includes case law, excursion to international legal organisations, interviews with practitioners and a moot court session. Contribution: A related disciplinary contribution, with a different object, method and assessment; no whole Maastricht module or professional qualification equivalence claimed.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Interdisciplinary study of contemporary societal challenges through the intersecting cultural domains of art, science/technology, media and politics” and “Critical, interdisciplinary humanities-and-qualitative-social-science analysis of cultural texts, artefacts, practices, discourses and institutions”.

Contribution: A related disciplinary contribution, with a different object, method and assessment; no whole Maastricht module or professional qualification equivalence claimed.. Contribution: A related disciplinary contribution, with a different object, method and assessment; no whole Maastricht module or professional qualification equivalence claimed.. basisLabels: Historical development of Western culture and thought from antiquity to the twenty-first century, tracing the deep historical roots of present-day societal problems
courseTraceability.rationale: Native American Histories This course introduces students to Native American history and life from the 19th through the 21st century.  It argues that power, fear, misogyny, education, genocide, and resilience shape the Indigenous past and present. Topics we explore include the “Stolen Lives” of Indian children forcibly taken from their homes and placed in Indian Boarding Schools from the 1830’s through the 1990’s; Murdered and Missing Indigenous Women and Girls in the twenty-first century; and the individual and community forms of cultural resistance and environmental regeneration that connect past with present and future generations. We learn from the Native American scholars and 2Spirit youth that speak to and with the class. Exchange of cultural and intellectual knowledge also happens when we work with Lakota students to address contemporary challenges. Legislation, memoir, novels, and Indigenous children’s stories are central to our studies. So are the analyses of contemporary music and artistic expressions and exhibitions, as well as Hollywood and Indigenous film featuring Native American histories and lives. Contribution: A related disciplinary contribution, with a different object, method and assessment; no whole Maastricht module or professional qualification equivalence claimed.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical development of Western culture and thought from antiquity to the twenty-first century, tracing the deep historical roots of present-day societal problems”.

notes.text: These qualified responses retain genuine cultural, historical, philosophical, literary and media analysis. Technical computing, organizational study and environmental science are companion subjects, not substitutes for cultural theory. Maastricht’s ethnography, discourse and conceptual-analysis progression and 16 EC thesis remain different.

Maastricht combines content courses with separately credited skills and a scaffolded proposal/thesis sequence. UCR distributes related work across whole courses; optional independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 EC. Neither its different format nor thematic similarity establishes degree or professional equivalence.

audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht Arts and Culture studies contemporary cultural and societal questions through history, philosophy, art, literature and qualitative social research. It connects art, science and technology, media and politics through content courses, paired skills and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three qualified UCR alternatives approach cultural history and the arts, digital culture and ethics, or environmental culture and governance. Each has substantive related study and different companion subjects. Maastricht’s integrated methods and research sequence remain distinct.
